title: cross-SDK stream resume + graceful token refresh bridge (python/ts/go)
author: Maya Singh
description: Motivation: long-lived streaming sessions occasionally encounter mid-stream 401/403 during token expiry/rotation. Clients either dropped the stream (losing partial results) or had to re-establish and reparse responses, causing UX roughness and higher error rates for interactive apps. This PR introduces a cross-SDK compatibility layer and ergonomics improvements to allow graceful token refresh and optional in-band resume semantics so higher-level applications can recover without full restart. Summary of changes: 1) wire-level: introduce an opt-in resume_token header and an optional resume handshake message for streaming transports. The contract is backward-compatible: servers not advertising resume support simply ignore the header. 2) auth: implement a LeakyTokenRefresh shim that transparently handles 401/reauth during an active stream and attempts a resume when the server supports it. 3) SDK ergonomics: Python adds Stream.as_context() to get automatic refresh + cleanup; TypeScript exposes AsyncIterable.withResume({timeout}) helper; Go adds StreamResumer interface and a small helper in the connection pool to retry with jittered backoff. 4) tests: new integrational mocks that simulate mid-stream expiry and validate exactly-once resume semantics for client-visible events. 5) versions: minor bumps to sdk packages to publish compatibility patches (python 1.8.0, typescript 2.4.3, go 0.9.2). Compatibility notes: the new resume header is optional, and servers must explicitly opt into resume behaviour. Existing SDKs will continue to work unchanged if not using the new helpers. Rollout plan: feature gated behind server-side flag for the first two weeks; telemetry added to monitor resume success/failure and any duplicated events. Checklist: - [x] design doc and sequences (linked) - [x] implementation across python/ts/go - [x] unit & integration tests - [x] e2e harness against mock token rotation - [x] docs snippets for SDKs - [x] version bumps and changelogs - [x] telemetry dashboards and alerts (QA)

review_comments: Liam O'Connor: Can we ensure resume_token can't be replayed? Suggest tying resume_token to connection-id and short TTL.
Maya Singh (author): Reply: added connection-id binding and enforce 5s TTL server-side in design; client includes connection checksum in header to reduce replay risk.
Priya Raman: Question: how does this interact with function-calling / structured responses mid-stream? We need to ensure partial structured frames are re-emitted exactly once.
Maya Singh (author): Reply: shrunk atomic frame unit boundary in transport; integration tests validate dedupe by frame-sequence id. Added note in docs.
Diego Alvarez: CI flaked on linux/py3.11 matrix; re-run fixed it. Please add a small test that asserts no .close() leak when resuming fails.
Maya Singh (author): Reply: added test and resource cleanup in Stream.as_context() implementation.
merge_outcome: Merged by squash via UI after approvals from all reviewers. No merge conflicts. Release branches updated for SDK packages.
release_notes: SDKs: add optional graceful streaming resume and transparent token-refresh helpers across Python/TypeScript/Go. Backward compatible; opt-in resume header required. Minor version bumps: python 1.8.0, typescript 2.4.3, go 0.9.2. See docs/sdk/streaming-resume.md for migration guide.
additional_notes: Telemetry: track resume_attempt, resume_success, resume_duplicate_detected. Rollout: server-side feature flag for 2w. Operations: monitor increase in dup events for first 48h after rollout. Security: resume tokens are short lived and bound to connection checksum to mitigate replay.
